items.where: NE street: two 11-storey dark brick towers rising over a continuous 4-storey brick street wing, the right tower box cantilevered over a set-back base
items.how: 3DBAG LoD2.2 shell massing, every rectangular wall rebuilt as a holed dark brick face (systemWall)

items.where: all upper storeys: punched French windows in red-brown frames with a low metal rail, singles and pairs in an irregular rhythm
items.how: 0.95 m singles with a rail strip and up to 1.7 m pairs at a 2.5 m bay pitch, a deterministic per-wall pattern with gaps (triangle budget)

items.where: top three storeys at the right corner of each tower: a large white-framed glazed stack; a long glazed stack on the inner tower faces
items.how: one 2x3 white-framed opening per tower face at its right end over the top three storeys, a five-storey stack on faces >= 20 m

items.where: ground storey along the street: timber-framed glazing with lime-green panels carrying large stair numbers 2, 3, 4, and red residential doors
items.how: 3.4 m bays of two-light timber-framed glazing, about one in seven with a green panel back, some red doors; numbers skipped as lettering under 1.5 m

items.where: under the left tower, about 41 m from the SE corner: a two-storey orange-framed entrance portal
items.how: 0.9 m deep opening with a 25 cm copper-orange frame and a transom bar

items.where: large white stair numbers 2, 3, 4 on the green ground panels

skip.note: numerals under 1.5 m, read as the green panel at riding distance

items.where: SW side seen over the 1920s houses in front: the same dark brick towers with punched windows and a glazed stack
items.how: same systemWall as the NE street

items.where: NW end: dark brick tower end with punched windows and white-framed glazing over a glazed ground storey, mostly behind trees
SE end: the top four storeys of the tower are a box cantilevered about 1 m over the lower storeys with a dark soffit
items.how: as the 3DBAG shell gives the overhang; the soffit is the shell roof face

items.where: SE ground storey: timber-framed glazing and lime-green glass panels with stair number 1
